READING

**1. Planning and construction timeline**

The application was validated 2026-08-14. Adding the three recorded outcomes and then 22 weeks of construction:

| Scenario | Consent | Culverstone open | Hallowbrand expires | Gap at Nethercote |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13-week target | 2026-11-10 | 2027-04-04 | 2027-11-30 | none |
| 34-week median | 2027-04-05 | 2027-09-07 | 2027-11-30 | none |
| 61-week slowest | 2027-10-12 | 2028-03-09 | 2027-11-30 | ~14 weeks |

In any outcome at or better than the median, the transition is clean: Culverstone opens in September 2027, nearly three months before Hallowbrand falls in. Only in a sub-median outcome does a Nethercote bridge arise. The worst case ever recorded produces a gap of roughly fourteen weeks — call it 3.5 months — between Hallowbrand expiry and Culverstone readiness.

---

**2. Dead mileage**

Culverstone is three miles further from Verrancombe Bridge. Each vehicle running the 44 network does one dead run out from depot to stand and one dead run back each operating day, so the additional dead mileage per vehicle is six miles per operating day.

22 vehicles × 313 days × 6 miles × £0.63 = **£26,029 per year**

That figure erodes the headline rent saving but does not eliminate it.

---

**3. The Faskally deposit and site tenure**

Paying the £40,000 deposit before 2026-12-05 holds the Culverstone site until 2028-06-30. Even in the worst recorded planning outcome, Culverstone is available from around 2028-03-09 — comfortably inside the hold. The deposit preserves the option through every scenario in the data set.

---

**4. Ten-year financial comparison**

*KESTERWICK annual operating cost once on site:*
Rent £118,000 + dead mileage £26,029 = **£144,029 per year**

*ARDENSHAW annual cost:* **£214,000 per year**

*Annual saving under KESTERWICK:* £69,971

*Over ten years:* £699,710

*One-off costs under KESTERWICK:*
- Faskally deposit: £40,000
- Culverstone works: £480,000
- Nethercote bridge, worst case only (3.5 months × £18,500): £64,750
- Total worst case: £584,750

*Net position over ten years:*

| Scenario | One-off | 10-yr saving | Net benefit of KESTERWICK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Median (no Nethercote) | £520,000 | £699,710 | +£179,710 |
| Slowest (Nethercote) | £584,750 | £699,710 | +£114,960 |

KESTERWICK is cheaper over the decade in every outcome the county's own history gives reason to expect. The capital outlay pays back inside the term in all scenarios.

---

**5. Cash and liquidity**

Current cash: £640,000. Undrawn facility: £200,000. Total liquidity: £840,000.

Deposit (December 2026): −£40,000 → £800,000 available.
Works (upon consent, say mid-2027 in the median case): −£480,000 → £320,000 available, plus ten months of operating cashflow accumulated between deposit and works payment.

The £480,000 capex is large relative to the cash position but does not exhaust it, and the undrawn facility provides an explicit buffer. Liquidity is tight, not broken; nothing here requires external financing on unfavourable terms.

---

**6. The bid — the strategic weight of the decision**

Bids for the next 44/44A term go in 2027-09-14 with depot cost as a fixed line. This is where the two courses diverge most sharply.

Under ARDENSHAW, that line reads £214,000.

Under KESTERWICK, the realistic bid cases are:

- *Median or better (consent before ~2027-09-07):* Planning decided months earlier; Culverstone ready around the bid date; depot cost priced at £144,029. The bid carries £69,971 a year less overhead than the ARDENSHAW alternative. On a multi-year contract running 22 vehicles that saving is real margin or, if passed through, competitive advantage.

- *Worst case (consent after bid date):* Planning consent is expected around 2027-10-12, four weeks after the bid deadline. At that point the operation is still at Hallowbrand (which runs to 2027-11-30), so the depot cost the business has actually been paying during the run-up to the bid is £141,000/year — the current lease rate. Consent is imminent; Culverstone opens ~2028-03-09, before the new contract period begins 2028-04-01. A competent submission prices the short Nethercote bridge and names Culverstone as the steady-state depot at £144,029. That is still a materially stronger number than £214,000.

The 44/44A network is the backbone of the business — 22 of 31 vehicles, 313 days a year. A depot cost £70,000 a year higher than necessary is a structural disadvantage in a competitively tendered market. Over a typical multi-year contract the cumulative exposure from an uncompetitive bid is far larger than the absolute rent differential suggests.

---

**7. The Nethercote and workshop risk**

The Nethercote yard has no workshop. If the worst case occurs, vehicles would need to go to a third-party workshop for the fourteen-week bridge. That is an operational nuisance and an extra cost that has not been quantified above. It is not, however, a novel problem for a 31-vehicle operation; the industry manages contract maintenance routinely. Fourteen weeks of outsourced servicing will cost money but is unlikely to cost £115,000 — the margin by which KESTERWICK beats ARDENSHAW even in the worst recorded scenario.

---

**8. The ARDENSHAW comfort is real but priced too high**

ARDENSHAW offers a workshop from signature, a known depot cost to the penny, and no dependence on Verrancombe's planning machinery. Those are genuine advantages. But the certainty they buy costs £96,000 a year in additional rent — £960,000 over the lease term — for a site the business will still not own at expiry. The decision is not whether certainty has value; it plainly does. The question is whether that certainty is worth £69,971 a year net of the dead mileage penalty. It is not.

---

**Summary**

KESTERWICK pays its own capital cost within the lease term in every scenario the county's planning record warrants expecting. It puts a lower fixed-cost line into the bid that is decisive in a tendered market. The planning and Nethercote risks are bounded, temporary, and survivable within the existing cash position. ARDENSHAW locks the business into the highest depot cost in its history for a decade, on a site it will not own, with a bid number that will be visible to every other tenderer.

---

READING
The deposit secures Culverstone through the worst planning outcome on record; the ten-year rent and dead-mileage arithmetic recovers the full capital outlay in all scenarios the county's own history supports; and the lower depot cost materially strengthens the 2027-09-14 bid at the point where ARDENSHAW's £214,000 becomes a permanent competitive liability in a tendered market.

CALL
KESTERWICK

GROUNDS
The combined effect of the ten-year rent differential and the lower fixed line it puts into the 44/44A bid outweighs every quantifiable cost and risk attached to the Culverstone route, including the worst planning delay on record.
